key_insight: Flexible modular robots combine movement and object manipulation in the same unit. By physically connecting, they form task-adaptive structures that cooperate to carry objects, cross gaps and navigate difficult terrain.
problem_solved: Robots with fixed shapes or separate movement and manipulation systems can struggle with tasks that require both physical adaptability and teamwork.
method: Use flexible tensegrity continuum robot modules that support both locomotion and manipulation.
Physically connect modules into different configurations suited to each task.
Coordinate connected modules for cooperative object transport, gap crossing and challenging-terrain navigation.
impact: The work offers an embodied platform for exploring how robot shape and cooperation can expand task capabilities. For AI/ML practitioners, it motivates adaptive control and multi-robot coordination that account for changing physical configurations.
visual_elements: Annotated module diagram highlighting its flexible structure and movement/manipulation capabilities.
Sequence showing individual modules connecting into task-specific configurations.
Three-panel task illustration: carrying an object, crossing a gap and traversing uneven terrain.
Capability icons linking locomotion, manipulation and cooperation.
paper_title: Tensegrity continuum robots enable task-adaptive morphologies for cooperative behaviours
paper_authors: Mahmud Hasan Saikot, Sydney Spiegel, Sudheera Akalanka Kariyawasam, Andrew Stefka, Josh Chrisler
